newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Rollovers dominate stock options.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Rollovers dominate stock options.

text.p: Rollovers of positions in January contracts, which expire today, into further out months dominated activity in the equity options market, traders said.
"It's been pretty hectic all around the board, people just rolling over and closing out (January options)," said Rod Jamieson, a vice president at EVEREN Securities.

He said volume in Sun Microsystems Inc and Intel Corp options, which had been the center of action in the past several days, remained robust in the wake of recent earnings-related trades, but the market's interest was more spread out today.
Traders said the market was calm on the whole because only index options and individual equity options expired, unlike the quarterly "triple-witching" months when S&P futures also expire.
They added that although this month's expiration was rather featureless, a notable amount of rollovers were into higher strike prices, with the market near record-high levels.

"I would say, from the direction of the market, a lot of the volume is from rolling up strike prices or at least closing it down so they're not subject to exercise," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer and Co.
He added, however that some trades in January contracts that were not being rolled over could reflect the market's bullishness.

For instance, volume in Sun Microsystems January 30 calls, the most heavily traded contract today with 11,864 contracts changing hands by mid-afternoon, far exceeded the total volume in contracts that would be used for rollovers, he noted.
While most of that was likely to have been profit-taking on speculative positions, there were also probably a lot of covered-call positions not being rolled over, Schwartz said.
"They may have closed out a substantial portion of these, leaving their stock holdings unhedged, looking for more appreciation over the next few months," he said.

In covered-call strategy, investors sell calls against their stock holdings to use the premium received as a cushion on the downside or as supplement profit when the stock makes small gains. But the strategy has limited upside profit potential because the stock would get called away if it rallied sharply.
Sun Microsystem stock, up 3/16 on the day at 31-1/4, had recently stemmed a three-month decline and rallied sharply on good earnings results.

Intel options also saw big volume, mainly on expiration related activity. But Jamieson said some selling came from traders trying to take advantage of relatively high implied volatility levels. Intel option premiums had been pumped up prior to the firm's earnings results earlier in the week.
"It (implied volatility) crashed when the numbers came out but...there are guys thinking it's still a little high," he said.
